The Company offers its own proprietary LFP battery solution, comprehensive EPC services, and innovative solutions aimed at improving grid operations, integrating clean energy, and contributing to a sustainable future. e-STORAGE has successfully implemented over 3.3 GWh DC of battery energy storage solutions in various locations, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and China. Position Title: Controls Engineer

Department: Engineering

Location: UK

Position Summary
The Controls Engineer will lead the implementation of BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) capable of ultra-fast response to dispatch commands and grid supply variations. This candidate must be familiar with power systems, utility generation, protection, and transmission systems, as well as modern industrial networks and utility communication protocols.

What You'll Be Doing as a Controls Engineer

• Review project contracts and vendor agreements for controls-related requirements and ensure alignment throughout project execution.

• Review and validate project design packages, including electrical drawings, data flow diagrams, network designs, signal mappings (analog, Modbus, DNP3), electrical power models, and control narratives.

• Maintain and organize technical documentation within SharePoint while coordinating documentation flow with vendors and project stakeholders.

• Develop batch scripts and automation tools to streamline data collection and improve operational efficiency.

• Serve as a key technical resource for customers, EPCs, utilities, equipment vendors, and internal project teams throughout project execution.

• Troubleshoot network and communications issues within VPN-secured environments.

• Respond to customer and operator requests regarding system modifications, troubleshooting, and control system enhancements.

• Support site commissioning activities and provide technical expertise for all controls-related tasks.

• Ensure all activities are performed in compliance with engineering standards, project requirements, safety protocols, and company policies.

What You'll Bring to The Position

• Educational background in Controls Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• Minimum of 3 years of experience working with industrial control systems within electrical generation, renewable energy, or similar power system environments is required.

• Experience working with inverter-based resources (IBR) such as Battery Energy Storage Systems, solar, or other renewable generation technologies

• Exposure to substations, protective relays, and transformers is preferred.

• Demonstrated experience with industrial communication protocols including Modbus, DNP3, and TCP/IP.

• Strong understanding of industrial networking, including IP addressing, subnetting, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and network communications.

• Experience with SCADA systems, plant control systems, or utility-scale automation.

• Excellent communication and problem-solving skills with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.

• Ability to travel up to 10–15% nationally and internationally to support project sites and vendor facilities.

​Compensation & Benefits:

Canadian Solar offers a competitive salary plus fully comprehensive benefits and performance bonus package based on an annual objective achievement. Our generous benefits package includes a 401(k) Retirement Plan, medical/dental/life/disability program, vacation, and sick days.

Canadian Solar Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE).  Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status.

• Experience working with inverter-based resources (IBR) such as Battery Energy Storage Systems, solar, or other renewable generation technologies

• Demonstrated experience with industrial communication protocols including Modbus, DNP3, and TCP/IP.

• Strong understanding of industrial networking, including IP addressing, subnetting, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and network communications.

Job Title:             Capital Markets Manager

Department:      Capital Markets

Location:             Canada (Global HQ) or US (NYC, Dallas, or Walnut Creek)

Reports To:         Solid reports to the Managing Director/Head of Capital Markets - Dotted Line reports to the President of CS Powertech and VP of Strategy and Innovation.

Position Summary:

Canadian Solar is building out its newly established Capital Markets function to support the financing and monetization needs of the company’s growing business and project portfolio. The manager will be a key member of this team, working closely with the Managing Director of Capital Markets to build the processes, tools, materials and operating infrastructure required to establish a scalable Capital Markets function.

The role will provide hands-on support and ownership across all public and private debt and equity financing, 45X tax credit monetization, financial modeling and transaction execution.

Responsibilities:

• Support and manage debt and equity financings for Canadian Solar Inc. and its subsidiaries, including project-level financings for manufacturing facilities across the U.S., Thailand, and other regions supporting the U.S. manufacturing supply chain, as well as corporate-level debt and equity capital raises for business units such as e-STORAGE, Module System Solutions (MSS), and other Canadian Solar subsidiaries.

• Execute financial analysis and prepare materials, including owning project and platform financial modeling, updating financing assumptions and scenarios, and preparing financing decks, investor materials, analyses and other transaction materials.

• Coordinate financing processes and diligence, including supporting lender, investor and tax credit buyer outreach; managing information flow; coordinating internal teams and external advisors; responding to diligence requests; maintaining data rooms; and tracking open items and deliverables.

• Execute transaction workstreams through closing, including maintaining transaction trackers, coordinating documentation and closing deliverables, and managing key milestones and deadlines.

• Assist in building the Capital Markets function and establish repeatable processes, including developing and improving corporate financial models, templates, processes, trackers, data rooms, financing materials and other tools and institutional knowledge to support lender and investor outreach, diligence, financing execution and 45X monetization.

• Support and manage the monetization of 45X tax credits associated with the US Manufacturing projects.

• Maintain relationships with banks, lenders, institutional investors, rating agencies, financial advisors, and other capital markets participants.

• Regular interaction with the different business leaders such as President of CS Powertech, CEO of CS Sunshine, and CFO of Canadian Solar Inc.

• The role is intended to be a core execution and team-building resource for the newly established Capital Markets function, with responsibility for both supporting active transactions as well as helping build the internal financial institutional infrastructure and processes needed as both the team and the business continue to grow.

Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field; MBA, CFA, or other advanced qualification is a plus.

• 5–8+ years of relevant experience in capital markets, investment banking, corporate finance, treasury, private credit, project finance, or a related field.

• Experience executing debt and/or equity financing transactions.

• Strong understanding of financial statements, valuation, financial modeling, capital structures, and corporate finance.

• Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills with strong PowerPoint/presentation capabilities.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.

• Ability to manage multiple complex transactions and priorities in a fast-paced, global environment.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to work effectively with senior executives and external financial institutions.

• Experience in renewable energy, energy storage, power, infrastructure, manufacturing, or technology is preferred.

• Experience working across international markets is a plus.

Lead and facilitate the generation of lessons learned from past projects and their implementation in future projects for continuous improvement in project quality

Identify and track quality Issues/observations/non-compliances, document and communicate their resolutions in accordance with the contractual requirements and the SSQP

Coordinate with and support engineering, project execution, and O&M teams in resolving equipment problems and proactively preventing performance issues

Implement and update project quality management system (PQMS) according to ISO standards to meet the ever-evolving BESS business development and project quality needs

Cultivate and exemplify a quality culture that focuses on awareness of personal impacts, openness, and willingness to learn and get better together, doing things safely and right the first time, and promoting continuous improvement

Educational background in Quality, Engineering, Project Management or a related field

•
At least 3 years' of experience in a similar role, preferably in the renewable energy industry or automotive industry

Capable of conducting RCA and tracking its progress to completion and driving suppliers for temporary containment and permanent corrective actions

•
Knowledge of manufacturing, function and O&M of inverters, transformers, or lithium-ion battery products; willing and able to learn new subjects and skills

•
Good at developing/maintaining strong relationships and working effectively with global cross functional cross-cultural colleagues, customers, suppliers, and contractors on quality matters

The Senior Power Electronics Control Engineer, specializes in Hardware-in-the-Loop simulation and validation of Power Conversion Systems (PCS) used in utility‑scale Battery Energy Storage Systems.

This role focuses on using real‑time digital simulators to emulate grids, inverters, batteries, and power stages in order to develop and validate control firmware, system‑level behavior, protection logic, and grid‑code compliance.

You will own the PCS HIL simulation environment, bridging power electronics, control algorithms, firmware, and system requirements to enable fast, repeatable, and certifiable testing.

Responsibilities:

• Design, develop, and maintain Hardware‑in‑the‑Loop (HIL) test environments for PCS and inverter control validation.

• Build real‑time PCS simulation models, including grid models, filters, transformers, battery models, and protection interfaces.

• Develop and validate inverter control algorithm firmware, protection strategies, and system behaviors under normal and abnormal operating conditions.

• Execute test cases covering grid-code compliant functionalities prior to certification testing.

• Support grid code compliance activities through documented test results and traceability.

• Expand scope of HIL platform to cover other equipment, technologies and system according to future development plan.

• Develop automated HIL test scripts and regression test suites to support continuous firmware and control validation.

• Integrate HIL testing into development workflows and release processes.

• Debug complex control and system‑level issues using real‑time waveforms, logs, and simulation data.

• Maintain professional documentation for HIL architectures, simulation models, test plans, and validation reports.

• Support root‑cause analysis for lab and field issues by reproducing scenarios in HIL.

• Conduct testing of the PCS hardware.

• Mentor junior engineers and support product lifecycle and field issue resolution.

Core Competencies & Technical Skills

• Strong experience with real‑time HIL simulation for power electronics or grid‑connected systems.

• Proficiency with HIL platforms such as OPAL‑RT, Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, RTDS, or similar.

• Experience building real‑time models for inverters, batteries, power systems and protection systems.

• Understanding of real‑time execution constraints, model fidelity, and latency considerations.

• Solid background of power converter, especially inverter architectures, and energy storage systems.

• Experience with converter control loops, digital protection mechanisms, and system‑level sequencing.

• Ability to interpret control block diagrams, firmware behavior, and electrical schematics.

• Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, Ethernet, SPI, UART, Modbus, and proprietary interfaces.

• Experience with test automation, scripting, or model‑based validation workflows.

• Familiarity with version control (GitHub/Bitbucket), documentation practices, and structured validation processes.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail in test development and result interpretation.

Required Qualifications and Skills:

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline. Advanced degrees in Power Electronics are preferred.

• 5+ years of professional experience in HIL testing, real‑time simulation, or PCS/inverter validation.

• Demonstrated experience validating power converters system using real-time simulators.

Job Description:

A Quality Technician ensures the quality and reliability of solar cells, raw materials, and components across specialized quality control (QC) areas. Reporting to the QC Supervisor or Quality Engineer, this role executes inspections, conducts tests, documents results, and supports issue resolution within a designated focus area (e.g., Incoming Quality Control, Outgoing Quality Control, Reliability Testing, Metrology, or In-Process Quality Control). Technicians adhere to standard operating procedures (SOPs), regulatory standards (e.g., ISO), and customer specifications to maintain consistent product quality.

Core Responsibilities:

• Adhere to SOPs, safety protocols, regulatory requirements (ISO 9001), and the company’s quality/environmental policies.

• Document test results, inspection data, and non-conformities accurately in quality management systems

• Report defects, discrepancies, or equipment issues to the QC Supervisor promptly.

• Maintain cleanliness and calibration of tools/equipment used in the assigned area.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams (other department) to address quality concerns.

• Participate in training programs to stay updated on processes, standards, and new technologies.

• Perform other quality-related duties assigned by the Quality Manager and/or Supervisor to support organizational quality objectives.

Specialized Responsibilities by Area

1. Incoming Quality Control (IQC) Technician

• Inspect incoming raw materials (e.g., silicon wafers, chemicals) to ensure they meet purchase orders and quality standards.

• Test materials (e.g., thickness, purity) using tools.

• Reject non-conforming materials and work with suppliers/procurement to resolve issues.

• Track records of incoming quality, including pass/fail rates and supplier performance.

2. Outgoing Quality Control (OQC) Technician

• Perform final checks on finished product batches to confirm they meet customer and internal standards.

• Test sample cells (e.g., efficiency, EL/PL imaging) from each production lot.

• Verify product packaging, labels, and shipping documents.

• Approve/reject batches based on results; escalate problematic lots to the QC Supervisor.

• Create quality reports for customers or internal teams.

3. Reliability Testing Technician

• Run tests on solar cells to check long-term performance and durability.

• Monitor test conditions, record data (e.g., efficiency loss), and document failures.

• Help analyze results to spot reliability trends or design flaws.

• Maintain test equipment (e.g., chambers) and ensure accurate environmental controls (temperature, humidity).

4. Metrology Technician

• Calibrate and maintain precision tools (e.g., EL/PL imagers, IV curve tracers).

• Conduct routine checks to ensure equipment accuracy and compliance with ISO 17025.

• Troubleshoot malfunctions and coordinate repairs with maintenance or vendors.

• Document calibration records and train others on proper tool use.

5. In-Process Quality Control (IPQC) Technician

• Monitor solar cell production at key stages.

• Conduct inline inspections using measuring instruments.

• Collect real-time process data and compare it to specifications.

• Alert production teams to deviations and help adjust processes to prevent defects.

• Track yield rates and identify defect trends at specific manufacturing step.

Qualifications & Skills

• Associate’s degree in Electrical Technology, Materials Science, or a related field (preferred).

• Minimum 3 years in quality control within manufacturing, with preference for solar cell fabrication, semiconductor, or renewable energy industries.

• Familiarity with the specific focus area (e.g., incoming inspections) is preferred.

• Quality management certifications (e.g., ASQ Certified Quality Technician) or specialized training (e.g., metrology, reliability testing) are a plus.

• Skilled with tools/equipment specific to the assigned area (e.g., imagers for OQC).

• Basic understanding of statistical process control (SPC) and quality metrics (e.g., CPK, yield).

• Ability to interpret technical drawings, spec sheets, and industry standards (ISO 9001).

• Proficient in office software (e.g., MS Excel for data analysis, Word for documentation).

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy in documentation.

• Effective verbal/written communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate cross-functionally.

• Basic problem-solving abilities to identify defects or process deviations.

• Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment, manage priorities, and follow instructions.

Working Conditions:

• Primarily works in a manufacturing facility, including cleanrooms, labs or controlled-environment production areas.

• Potential exposure to low-level chemicals or equipment noise; appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) is provided and required.

• This role works 12-hour shifts, which may include day, evening, or night shifts, depending on production needs. Occasional overtime may be needed to support production deadlines, urgent quality issue resolution, audit preparations or urgent tasks.

• May involve standing for extended periods, moving between workstations, and lifting.

Duties & Responsibilities

• Partner with manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain, EHS, and operations teams to document existing processes and develop standardized procedures.

• Interview subject matter experts and observe operational activities to accurately capture workflows and process requirements.

• Translate complex manufacturing, engineering, and operational processes into clear, user-friendly documentation.

• Develop process flow diagrams, workflow charts, visual work instructions, and training materials to improve knowledge transfer and operational consistency.

• Support documentation efforts related to ISO standards, quality systems, audits, compliance requirements, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Establish document control standards, version management practices, and document governance processes.

• Collaborate with global teams to standardize documentation formats, templates, and best practices across multiple business units and manufacturing facilities.

• Review and update existing documentation to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with operational changes.

• Support onboarding and workforce training initiatives through development of instructional and reference materials.

• Assist with process improvement projects by documenting current-state and future-state workflows.

• Manage multiple documentation projects simultaneously while meeting established timelines and quality standards.

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Technical Writing, Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Business, Communications, or a related field preferred.

• 3+ years of experience in technical writing, process documentation, manufacturing operations, quality systems, engineering documentation, or a related discipline.

• Experience documenting manufacturing processes, SOPs, work instructions, process flows, or quality procedures.

• Strong ability to gather information through interviews, process observation, and stakeholder collaboration.

• Exceptional written communication, editing, and document organization skills.

• Experience creating process maps, workflow diagrams, and visual documentation.

• Familiarity with manufacturing environments, production operations, quality management systems, or industrial processes.

• Working knowledge of ISO standards, document control systems, continuous improvement methodologies, or operational excellence programs preferred.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Visio, SharePoint, and documentation management systems.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality deliverables.

Position Title: Senior SAP S/4HANA PCE Operations & Integration Lead
Department: IT Applications
Location: Kitchener, Ontario or Dallas, TX

This position requires regular onsite/in-office attendance.

Position Summary
Sunshine Group is seeking an experienced SAP S/4HANA PCE Operations & Integration Lead to support the production operation, governance, and continuous improvement of the group SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition landscape.

This is not a traditional infrastructure-heavy SAP Basis role. The SAP environment is hosted and managed through SAP S/4HANA PCE, so the successful candidate will focus on production monitoring, incident triage, transport and release coordination, SAP service-provider coordination, integration monitoring, and operational governance.

The ideal candidate has strong SAP Basis knowledge, practical experience supporting SAP production environments, hands-on exposure to SAP Transport Management, strong troubleshooting skills, and experience with SAP CPI / SAP Cloud Integration / SAP Integration Suite. SAP BTP experience is highly preferred, as Sunshine Group plans to expand and upgrade BTP capabilities over time.
Duties & Responsibilities

SAP S/4HANA PCE Production Operations & Governance

• Support day-to-day production operations for the SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition landscape serving Sunshine Group.

• Monitor system availability, performance, capacity indicators, jobs, interfaces, RFCs, queues, dumps, spool, update processing, and overall system health.

• Perform first-level SAP technical triage and coordinate escalation to SAP PCE, managed service providers, infrastructure teams, functional teams, and business stakeholders as needed.

• Review and coordinate SAP maintenance windows, planned downtime, patching schedules, upgrades, service requests, incident tickets, and root-cause-analysis reports.

• Maintain production support procedures, escalation paths, monitoring checklists, operational

Production Incident Management & Troubleshooting

• Troubleshoot SAP production issues using strong Basis knowledge and standard SAP monitoring tools and transactions.

• Analyze common SAP technical issues including dumps, failed jobs, RFC/connectivity failures, interface errors, queues, locks, update failures, spool issues, certificate issues, and user access problems.

• Coordinate cross-functional incident response across SAP, integration, functional, infrastructure, cloud operations, and business teams.

• Drive timely issue resolution, business communication, post-incident review, and preventive action tracking.

• Support production readiness, cutover, go-live, and hyper-care activities for new SAP capabilities and business rollouts.

Transport, Release & Change Management

• Manage and coordinate SAP Transport Management System activities across Development, QA, and Production environments.

• Validate transport sequencing, dependencies, approvals, release timing, testing status, and production change-control requirements.

• Coordinate normal releases, emergency transports, production fixes, and post-release validation with functional, development, integration, and business teams.

• Support release calendars, change advisory reviews, blackout periods, backout planning, and audit evidence collection for production changes.

• Ensure transport and release processes are well documented, controlled, repeatable, and aligned with IT governance expectations.

Migration, Refresh, Upgrade & Hypercare Support

•    Support SAP migration, upgrade, system refresh, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization activities from a customer-side technical operations perspective.

• Coordinate with SAP PCE / managed service providers for system refreshes, client copies, environment readiness, backup validation, disaster recovery testing, and technical maintenance activities.

• Perform customer-side validation after refreshes, upgrades, maintenance windows, and production changes.

• Help ensure system availability, business continuity, and operational readiness during major SAP lifecycle events.

SAP CPI / Cloud Integration / Integration Suite Operations

• Support SAP integration operations using SAP CPI / SAP Cloud Integration / SAP Integration Suite as the integration gateway for SAP and external systems.

• Monitor integration flows, message failures, queues, connectivity issues, certificates, authentication, destinations, and interface exceptions.

• Coordinate troubleshooting across SAP S/4HANA, CPI / Integration Suite, external applications, functional teams, vendors, and business users.

• Support integration testing, migration, cutover, post-go-live stabilization, and interface monitoring procedures.

• Maintain integration support documentation, escalation paths, and operational runbooks for critical interfaces.

SAP BTP Readiness & Future Platform Support

• Support the future SAP BTP roadmap, including BTP upgrade planning, operational readiness, integration capabilities, and platform governance.

• Work with internal teams and external partners on SAP BTP subaccounts, connectivity, security roles, Cloud Connector, destinations, certificates, and integration monitoring as needed.

• Help define support procedures and governance models for BTP-based services as Sunshine Group expands its SAP cloud platform capabilities.

SAP Security, User Administration & Compliance Support

• Support SAP user administration, role assignments, authorization troubleshooting, and access lifecycle activities.

• Use working knowledge of PFCG roles, authorization objects, and authorization trace tools to analyze access issues.

• Support periodic user access reviews, audit evidence collection, security compliance activities, and basic Segregation of Duties concepts.

• Collaborate with business process owners, functional teams, and security teams to maintain controlled and auditable access practices.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience will also be considered.

• 5+ years of SAP Basis, SAP technical operations, or SAP production support experience.

• Experience supporting SAP S/4HANA production environments.

• Experience working with SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition, RISE with SAP, SAP managed cloud, or other hosted SAP environments.

• Strong SAP Basis knowledge, including system monitoring, troubleshooting, background jobs, dumps, RFCs, spool, queues, update processing, user administration, and interface monitoring.

• Strong experience with SAP Transport Management System, including Dev / QA / Production transport flow, release coordination, dependency management, emergency transports, and production change control.

• Experience coordinating with SAP, managed service providers, infrastructure teams, functional teams, developers, integration teams, and business users during production incidents and planned changes.

• Experience supporting SAP migrations, upgrades, system refreshes, cutover, and hyper-care activities.

• Experience with SAP CPI / SAP Cloud Integration / SAP Integration Suite, including interface monitoring and troubleshooting.

• Working knowledge of SAP security roles, PFCG, authorization troubleshooting, user provisioning, and audit support.

• Strong documentation, communication, stakeholder-management, incident-management, and root-cause-analysis skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

• SAP BTP experience, especially SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration, Cloud Connector, subaccounts, destinations, certificates, connectivity, and security roles.

• Experience with SAP Cloud ALM, SAP Solution Manager, or similar SAP monitoring and application lifecycle management tools.

• Experience with SAP Fiori administration, SAP Gateway, and Fiori Launchpad configuration.

• Experience supporting manufacturing, supply chain, finance, sales, or power electronics business processes in SAP.

• Experience with ITIL-based incident, problem, change, and release-management processes.

• Basic scripting or automation knowledge using PowerShell, Bash, Python, or similar tools is a plus.

• SAP certification in S/4HANA, BTP, Integration Suite, or Basis-related areas is a plus.

Role Title: Senior Power Systems Technician

Team: Power Systems Team | UK LTSA Operations

Reports to: High Voltage Technical Manager (Regional)

Region: South / North / Central (UK)

Role type: Field-based, senior technical role

Purpose

Acts as the regional senior technical specialist for power systems and product commissioning across the UK BESS fleet. Leads product commissioning of e-STORAGE products (SolBank, string inverters, MVSkids etc) to OEM standard, leads HV/MV maintenance and safety activities across e-STORAGE and third-party fleets (i.e. SMA, Power Electronics) and develops the competency of the wider service team to support HV/MV works.

Scope Definition: Product Commissioning

This role leads product commissioning of e-STORAGE products: commissioning of e-STORAGE power conversion and MV equipment to OEM standard, including first power-on initialization parameters, product-level testing, and return-to-service. The site Commissioning (Cx) team retains overall site and project commissioning ownership, including the energisation programme, grid compliance and G99 testing, punch lists, and client handover. The Power Systems Technician works within the site Cx team's sequence: the Cx team owns the programme and the date; Power Systems owns the product Cx, safety documents, and product-level sign-off within it.

MV/HV Authorisation & Control of Work

Control of work and HV authorisation are determined by contract and project phase:

• During commissioning, the EPC (or Principal Contractor) is responsible for site control of work and HV authorisation. This role operates within the EPC's safe system of work and provides product-level expertise.

• During LTSA operations, the HV authorisation and control-of-work model is defined in each contract and varies by site (client-appointed, third-party, or CSE-held). This role provides the trained, competent personnel for appointment where CSE holds or is delegated that responsibility.

• Where a third party holds HV authorisation for a site, this role coordinates, supervises interfaces, and delivers the product-level technical work within their control regime.

Key Responsibilities

Product Commissioning (e-STORAGE products)

• Lead product commissioning of e-STORAGE products across UK LTSA sites (SolBank, string inverters, MVSkids and associated MV plant) to OEM standard and project scope.

• Own and set first power-on initialization parameters (OEM-trained personnel requirement per product manuals); incorrect settings risk equipment damage and certification non-compliance.

• Own product commissioning standards, procedures, test records, and documentation packs; ensure consistency across all UK projects.

• Provide product-level technical support to the site Cx team during energisation.

• Support the site Cx team during SAT and witness testing; provide product-level technical sign-off.

HV/MV Operations & Safety

• Competent for appointment to carry out MV/HV isolations, earthing, and safety document duties under the prevailing site safe system of work, as a mandatory precursor to intrusive PM/CM works. Site HV authorisation arrangements are defined per contract and phase (see MV/HV Authorisation & Control of Work).

• Carry out operational HV/MV switching during the service phase, including switching for planned PM outages, CM interventions, and restoration on return to service, where CSE holds control of work under the contract.

• Provide HV/MV support to the service team during PM and CM activities: isolations, earthing, switching, and safe access where service team work interfaces with HV/MV plant.

• Lead HV/MV preventative maintenance across CSE, SMA and Power Electronics MV skids, RMUs, transformers, and protection systems per OEM schedules.

• Lead corrective maintenance and fault investigation on HV/MV equipment: root cause analysis, rectification and return to service.

• Provide safety leadership and oversight for all HV/MV activities in region, including supervision of third-party HV contractors where used.

Technical Expertise & Capability Building

• Subject-matter expert across all inverter platforms (CSE string inverters, SMA, Power Electronics) for HV/MV maintenance activities; product commissioning expertise applies to e-STORAGE products.

• Assess and develop service team competency for HV/MV support roles; deliver toolbox talks, training, and authorisation recommendations.

• Feed field learnings back into standards, RAMS/SOPs, and OEM escalations.

Out of Scope

• Routine non-HV/MV maintenance (LV PM, BESS enclosure servicing, HVAC, general CM). This is delivered by the regional service team, with this role providing HV oversight only where work interfaces with HV/MV plant.

Requirements

• Trained and competent for MV/HV activities to 33kV; capable of appointment under company or client operational rules as contracts require.

• Time-served electrical background with utility-scale BESS or solar commissioning experience.

• Working knowledge of MV switchgear, transformers, and protection systems.

• Familiarity with G99 requirements sufficient to support the site Cx team during compliance testing.

• Full UK driving licence; regional and occasional national travel.

Production Leadership & Operations

• Supervise and coordinate daily production activities to ensure safe, efficient, and uninterrupted operations.

Process Knowledge & Capacity Management

• Line clearance time.

• Time required from first wafer input to final product output.

• Production recovery timelines to support manpower planning, production scheduling, and cross-functional coordination.

• Analyze root causes using structured problem-solving methodologies and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to increase throughput, improve yield, reduce downtime, and enhance Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

• Monitor and optimize material consumption while minimizing material waste and process losses.

• Establish and maintain robust inventory control, reconciliation, and verification procedures to ensure material traceability and inventory integrity.

• Set performance goals and deadlines that align with company objectives and effectively communicate expectations to team members.

• Build a high-performing team through leadership, coaching, mentoring, and employee development.

• Foster positive working relationships while promoting employee engagement, accountability, and continuous learning.

• Identify performance gaps and implement development plans to improve team capability and operational excellence.

• Self-motivated, results-driven, and solution-oriented.

• Mandarin language skills are an asset but not required.

Position Summary:

The Commissioning Engineer is part of a cross functional team that focuses on executing battery storage projects with market leading technologies. The Commissioning Engineer is responsible for testing and commissioning oversight activities of Battery Energy System Storage (BESS) projects from Pre-Commissioning phase through to Substantial Completion to ensure successful execution and operation of the BESS project. The Commissioning Engineer is expected to spend over 75% of his or her time at the project site.

Responsibilities:

Project Planning (remote):

• Participate in meetings with owner, operation and maintenance, design, and construction personnel to understand project goals and schedule to ensure proper coordination of commissioning activities.

• Assist the Commissioning Manager in Preparing commissioning plans, specifications and checklist and functional test documentation based on client and company standards.

• Review project documents and preliminary designs to identify gaps in scope and responsibility to ensure project success. This requires a comprehensive understanding of engineering, construction, and permitting concepts.

Project Commissioning (on site):

• Responsible for executional commissioning activities, which requires understanding/managing the scope, stakeholders and schedule and keeping all parties in sync.

• Interface with internal customers (commissioning manager, project manager, construction manager) and external customers (utilities, AHJs, contractors, end customers) to ensure consistent communication.

• Manage equipment supplier and host daily plan of day (POD) with each supplier to have them report progress and schedule their work.

• Review equipment Factory Acceptance Test procedures and reports.

• Perform site visits to coordinate commissioning plan, schedules, and check list to ensure all commissioning activities and performance testing are executed efficiently.

• Inspect construction work and support the resolution of installation and commissioning technical issues.

• Suggest improvement in commissioning execution plan or procedures/processes based on lessons learned.

• Assist in coordinating and training operation and maintenance personnel to maintain commissioned systems and perform a continuous commissioning program.

Other:

• Maintain and develop key strategic relationships with major vendors, suppliers, and contractors throughout the energy storage industry.

• Support value-engineering and process improvements efforts by sharing project specific lessons learned.

Qualifications and Experience Requirements:

• BS in an engineering field or equivalent experience/practical knowledge.

• 5-10 years of relevant experience in commissioning and/or systems engineering within Energy Storage integrator or EPC contractor.

• Direct experience in battery storage systems, medium voltage stations, and/or related products/systems.

• Proficient in the specification, technical bid analysis and procurement of major equipment such as inverters, transformers, switchgear etc...

• Proficient is SCADA systems and associated communication protocols.

• Must have a sound understanding of commissioning and testing of Energy Storage projects.

• Practical hands-on experience in system engineering and solid understanding of related regulatory standards including local code compliance.

• A go-getter professional with a can-do attitude - setting aggressive, measurable goals and objectives for him/herself and prepared to be measured against them.

• A dynamic professional and the ability to positively interact and collaborate with a diverse group of people at all levels and disciplines and capable of standing in front of key clients, thinking on his/her feet, and making sound decisions within compressed timelines.

• An excellent time manager, able to balance multiple projects and prioritize a broad variety of issues, initiatives, and objectives concurrently.

• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships internally and externally with staff, management, clients, suppliers, community partners and external stakeholders.

• Demonstrated sound judgment and the ability to be decisive in crisis situations.

• Demonstrated independent thinking, initiative, and creativity.

• Ability to work flexible hours (evenings, weekends) and travel to project sites as required

Position Title: Hardware Engineer
Department: Inverter Firmware
Compensation: $87,000 - $135,000 + annual bonus
Reports To: Director of Digital Inverter Firmware
Location: Kitchener, ON (onsite)

Who We Are

CS Digital is a digital technology startup focused on providing state-of-the-art digital technology for power solutions. Our first goal is to build a North American based inverter control board, firmware and energy station controller for the BESS industry to compliment Canadian Solar’s String Power Conversion System Medium Voltage Skid for the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) industry.

About the Role:

The PCB Designer / Hardware Engineer is responsible for the schematic design, PCB layout, and documentation of high‑reliability electronic hardware used in inverters, batteries, and energy storage systems. This role requires hands‑on experience across the full hardware design lifecycle, from schematic capture and component selection through layout, prototype bring‑up, and production release.

You will work closely with power electronics, firmware, FPGA, systems, and mechanical teams to deliver robust, certifiable, and manufacturable hardware for utility‑scale BESS applications.

Responsibilities:

• Translate system‑level, functional, and regulatory requirements into complete and well‑documented schematic designs.

• Design and develop electrical schematics for inverter control boards, power interface boards, sensing circuits, communication interfaces, and auxiliary hardware.

• Perform component selection for digital, mixed‑signal, and power‑related circuits, considering performance, availability, reliability, and cost.

• Define hardware architecture and electrical interfaces between PCBs, power stages, FPGA/DSP/MCUs, sensors, and external systems.

• Design multilayer PCB layouts for energy storage and inverter applications.

• Perform component placement and routing for high-speed signal, mixed‑signal, high‑power, and high‑voltage designs, ensuring optimal signal integrity, EMI/EMC, and thermal performance.

• Apply best practices and standard compliance (UL, IEC) for creepage, clearance, isolation barriers, grounding, and shielding.

• Prepare and maintain complete manufacturing deliverables, including schematic packages, PCB layouts, stack‑ups, Gerbers, BOMs, pick‑and‑place files, and assembly drawings.

• Support prototype bring‑up, board testing, debugging, and root‑cause analysis in the lab.

• Participate in design reviews and incorporate feedback to improve reliability, manufacturability, and cost.

• Support ECOs, cost‑down activities, supplier coordination, and field issue investigations during the product lifecycle.

Required Qualifications and Skills:

• Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering Technology, or a related discipline.

• 5+ years of professional experience in schematic design and PCB layout for embedded systems, power electronics, or industrial equipment.

• Demonstrated experience designing hardware for power converters, or other high‑reliability electronic systems.

• Experience supporting designs subject to safety and regulatory standards such as UL, IEC, or equivalent certifications.

• Hands‑on experience supporting prototype builds, lab validation, and production release.

• Strong analytical, problem‑solving, documentation, and technical communication skills.

• Solid understanding of power supply design, signal conditioning, isolation techniques, and protection circuitry.

• Ability to read, create, and review complex schematics and PCB layout with attention to safety, robustness, and certifiability

• Strong experience designing schematics for digital, mixed‑signal, and power electronics systems.

• Strong understanding of signal integrity, EMI/EMC, creepage, and clearance requirements.

• Experience with professional PCB CAD tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or equivalent.

• Capability to create and manage schematic symbols, footprints, and PCB libraries.

• Experience working in cross‑functional engineering teams across hardware, firmware, FPGA, and mechanical disciplines.

• Familiarity with version control, ECO processes, and structured hardware release workflows.

• Experience working in cross‑functional engineering teams across hardware, firmware, FPGA, and mechanical disciplines

• Strong documentation discipline and attention to detail.

• Validate software/firmware updates in coordination with vendors, the site service team, and relevant stakeholders to confirm documented changes and no unintended consequences are introduced. Coordinate subsequent rollouts with the appropriate site service teams.

• Effectively communicate issues to the appropriate vendor and stakeholders to ensure resolutions are identified and implemented.

• Support performance testing as required under individual contracts for each facility.

• Contribute to fleet wide efforts for improving the efficacy of monitoring and analysis processes and tools.

• Collaborate with internal teams to provide input to improve performance across the business from applications and design to project execution and commissioning to service.

• Provide documentation of issues and resolutions for tracking, knowledge sharing, and internal and external communications.

• Ensure all activities are performed in compliance with safety protocols, engineering standards, and company policies.

• Ability to execute projects and tasks in parallel, self-directed, highly detail-oriented, organized and flexible

• Experience in commissioning, performance testing, maintenance, and/or design of BESS or other power generating facilities

• Knowledge and experience with SCADA protocols (i.e. DNP3 and Modbus)

Job Title: Security Specialist, I
Department: Security
Reports to: Security Supervisor

Job Description:
The Security Specialist is responsible for the end-to-end management of internal and external investigations, threat assessments, and the mitigation of risks to corporate assets, intellectual property, and personnel. This role moves beyond oversight to the active detection, analysis, and resolution of security breaches and policy violations within the Jeffersonville manufacturing site and professional offices.

Primary Responsibilities:
Strategic Security Responsibilities and Processes
• Lead complex investigations into theft, fraud, workplace violence, and
unauthorized access. Document findings through comprehensive
investigative reports suitable for senior leadership or legal proceedings.
• Leverage site digital card access logs, CCTV systems, and network activity
audits to reconstruct timelines of security incidents and identify responsible
parties.
• Execute strategies to identify "shrinkage" or loss in technology hardware and
equipment inventories, conducting deep-dive audits where discrepancies
are found.
• Conduct professional interviews with witnesses, victims, and subjects of
investigations, maintaining strict adherence to legal standards and corporate
ethics.
• Act as the primary point of contact for local law enforcement during criminal
investigations, ensuring evidence is preserved and chain of custody is
maintained.
• Conduct targeted security audits that simulate "adversary" tactics to identify
weaknesses in perimeter fencing, entrance gates, and high-value storage
areas.
• Refine contingency plans for security breaches (e.g., unauthorized access or
data exfiltration) to include formal "Post-Incident Reviews" (PIRs) that drive
policy changes.
• Analyze trends from routine daily security reports to identify emerging threats
before they result in a site violation.

Qualifications and Experience:
• Minimum 2+ years of overall security investigative experience
• Proficient in utilizing various computer software, including MS Office,
security management platforms, and incident reporting tools.
• Training with OSHA requirements and/or specialized site security training is
desirable.
• Familiarity with ISO compliance related to security desirable.
• High school diploma required.

Job Description:

The Quality Engineer is responsible for ensuring that products and processes meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role involves developing and implementing quality assurance procedures, conducting inspections and tests, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to resolve quality issues and drive continuous improvement. Assist Quality Manager in developing colleagues, writing SOPs, and improving operations.

Responsibilities:

• Quality Assurance:

• Develop and implement quality assurance policies, procedures, and standards.

• Conduct regular inspections and testing of products and processes to ensure compliance with quality specifications.

• Review and analyze quality data and metrics to identify trends, issues, and opportunities for improvement.

• Monitor and ensure compliances for in-process setting and requirement.

• Ensure outgoing products meet the specification requirements

• ISO ownership. To ensure all documentation in-place.

• Process Improvement:

• Collaborate with engineering and production teams to develop and implement process improvements aimed at enhancing product quality and efficiency.

• Use quality improvement methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma, Lean) to drive continuous improvement initiatives.

• Conduct root cause analysis of quality issues and implements corrective and preventive actions.

• Documentation and Reporting:

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation of quality assurance activities, including inspection reports, test results, and process changes.

• Prepare and present detailed reports on quality performance, trends, and improvement initiatives.

• Ensure that all quality-related documentation complies with industry regulations and standards.

• Supplier Quality Management:

• Evaluate and monitor the quality of materials and components provided by suppliers.

• Conduct supplier audits and assessments to ensure compliance with quality standards.

• Work with suppliers to resolve quality issues and implement improvements.

• Compliance and Regulatory Requirements:

• Ensure that products and processes comply with relevant industry standards and regulatory requirements.

• Stay updated on changes to regulations and standards affecting quality assurance practices.

• Prepare and facilitate regulatory audits and inspections as required.

• Training and Support:

• Provide training and guidance to production staff on quality standards, procedures, and best practices.

• Support the development and implementation of quality training programs.

• Assist in the resolution of quality-related issues and provide technical support to teams.

• Quality Control:

• Develop and maintain quality control plans and procedures.

• Oversee the calibration and maintenance of quality control equipment.

• Ensure that quality control measures are effectively integrated into production processes.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Quality Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Electrical & Electronics Engineering, Material Engineering, Chemical Engineering or a related field; master’s preferred.
